keep it to yourself phrase

also keep this to yourself, keep it a secret, between you and me, don’t tell anyone

classical

Cic. Att. 4.15.6: vērum haec tū tēcum habētō (Lewis & Short), s.v. habeō
Cic. Fam. 7.25.2: sēcrētō hoc audī, tēcum habētō, nē Apellae quidem lībertō tuō dīxeris (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 101

Haec tū tēcum habētō.

future imperative of habeō, with tēcum

keep this to yourself

Cicero’s way of sharing a secret in a letter. The future imperative habētō is the form of standing instructions.

Examples

  • sēcrētō hoc audī, tēcum habētō, nē Apellae quidem lībertō tuō dīxeris

    hear this in confidence and keep it to yourself; don’t tell even your freedman ApellaCic. Fam. 7.25.2 (Lewis & Short, s.v. habeō)

See also mystery.

SourcesLewis & Short: habeo
